claims.text: The proposed alloy class consists of homogeneous single-phase solid solutions containing at least five elements at no less than 5 at.% each.
Local lattice-distortion magnitude controls the superconducting transition temperature in this alloy class.
Differences in constituent atomic radii produce local lattice distortion.
The proposed starting material is a Nb-Ta-based refractory alloy having a random solid-solution structure.
The proposed Nb-Ta-based starting material is superconducting.
The starting material has a moderate level of lattice distortion.
The starting material has a known superconducting transition temperature.
Composition can be adjusted to vary atomic-size mismatch while holding overall valence electron count constant.
Increasing atomic-size mismatch increases local lattice distortion.
Greater local lattice distortion disrupts characteristic phonon modes.
Disruption of phonon modes reduces electron-phonon coupling efficiency.
Electron-phonon coupling is critical for Cooper-pair formation in the proposed alloys.
Reduced electron-phonon coupling lowers the superconducting transition temperature.
At constant valence electron count, alloys with greater measured atomic-size mismatch and lattice distortion will have lower transition temperatures than lower-distortion baseline alloys.
The proposed relationship is restricted to homogeneous single-phase solid solutions.
The proposed relationship may not apply to partially ordered alloys or systems dominated by strong electron correlations.
Detailed phonon spectra and minor secondary phases may independently influence the transition temperature.
The quantitative relationship between lattice-distortion magnitude and transition temperature is not established.
